Added and committed two regression tests covering the declaration load failures:

- A child declaration with an explicit ultimate payer loads without incorrectly requiring a selected parent payer.
- A company number stays paired with the `Company` donor kind when funder observations are grouped.

Both tests pass. Each also failed when I temporarily restored its original bug, confirming they catch the regressions. Formatting passed, and I updated [PR #26](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/26) with the test results.

The changes are committed on `fix/declaration-loader-parent-basis-20261008` as `c3640b0`. The local `todo.md` remains uncommitted. This follows the root-cause and behavior-focused testing principles: the tests exercise the loader’s observable results and demonstrate that each original failure is detected.

</image>

explain why hsbc is not deduplicated here:

[Image #1]

<image name=[Image #1] path="/var/folders/cz/rswsvzmn2998q95j0r32bkyh0000gn/T/codex-clipboard-mrZd1q.png">

</image>

please also investigate why teh unite union still has several duplicates:

[Image #1]

The resolver keeps both organizations separate when the evidence doesn’t meet its merge rules. Search then ranks each stored funder record independently, so it can show several related names together.

- **HSBC:** The two bank names differ only in capitalization and normalize to the same name. One pair with the same normalized address was merged. Another pair had a comma difference in the stored address, which the resolver treated as an address disagreement and rejected. The CEO-named record has a different name and role; its match remained in review. Its reported company number, `9928412`, is seven characters, so it doesn’t qualify as a company identity anchor. These decisions appear in the [local run’s pair decisions](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/data/01a11ac3-40f7-765f-8040-33e2c918a342/resolved/declarations/pair_decisions.parquet). The [resolver rules](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:72) require stronger evidence across roles, and require company numbers to be eight characters [to use as an anchor](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:38).

- **Unite:** Names such as `Unite`, `Unite Union`, and `Unite the Union` are not exact normalized matches, so they don’t qualify for the resolver’s exact-name donor rule. For example, `Unite Union` and `Unite` share a donor role and address, but their pair was left in review because their names differ. Regional entries also have different recorded addresses; some comparisons were rejected on that basis. The [local pair decisions](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/data/01a11ac3-40f7-765f-8040-33e2c918a342/resolved/declarations/pair_decisions.parquet) show these outcomes. The written [resolution policy](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/docs/funder-resolution-design.md:45) explicitly leaves fuzzy-name and alias matches without an automatic merge rule.

The search query returns qualifying funder rows by name or alias and rank; it doesn’t combine similar rows at display time ([search query](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:22)). The loader creates records from the resolver’s identity groups ([loader](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:394)).

One test is easy to misread: `shows_no_hsbc_duplicates` checks that each exact HSBC spelling appears once. It still expects the three spellings as separate results; it does not verify that they resolve to one HSBC identity ([test](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/integration.rs:30)).

Whether Unite’s regional offices and Parliamentary Staff Branch should be merged under one parent identity is still an open domain decision; the data alone doesn’t establish that. I found no HSBC-specific deduplication ticket or relevant Google Drive document.

as far as i'm concerned, the deduplication work is far from complete. If we can't resolve those two differently spelled HSBC records or most of the unite unions then our pipeline is not working. We did a LOT of component extraction in the cleaning. What purpose does this serve?

Your concern is justified. The cleaner does substantial name-feature extraction, but the current resolver barely uses it. **Those extracted components do not drive identity matching today**, so they cannot prevent the HSBC and Unite duplicates you found.

The cleaning stage records features such as `organisation_core`, initials, acronym expansions, and explicit trading-as aliases. The docs describe them as “candidates for future resolution,” not identity keys ([feature docs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/docs/declaration-cleaning.md:63)). But when data moves into resolution, its `Observation` keeps only the normalized name, address, role, donor kind, and company number ([resolution input](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/input.rs:7)). The scorer receives just name and address, and its model compares only those two fields ([model](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/resolution/exposed_resolution/model.json:18)). The richer features are dropped before matching.

That explains the examples:

- For **HSBC**, case normalization already makes `PLC` and `plc` match. One pair merged; another was rejected because its normalized address includes a comma difference. The CEO-named record has a different name and role, and its reported company number does not meet the resolver’s format rule.
- For **Unite**, `Unite`, `Unite Union`, and `Unite the Union` remain different normalized names. The current resolver leaves those fuzzy variants for review. The extracted organisation features do not define those names as aliases, and the resolver does not consume them anyway.

There is a useful role for this extraction: it preserves source evidence and makes structured signals available for a more capable matcher. But **availability is not use**. Search aliases are also gathered only *after* observations have been assigned the same identity, so they help find an existing record; they cannot bring separate records together ([loader](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:406)).

So the honest answer is that the pipeline has a feature-rich cleaning stage and a conservative, much narrower resolution stage. If the goal is reliable entity deduplication across spelling variants, abbreviations, role differences, and address formatting, the current implementation does not meet it. The extracted components are groundwork for that behavior, not proof that the behavior exists.
exactly  this is pretty inconsistent. lets move the resolution step to be looser. Think about the user here.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/arena-loose-resolution/candidate-evidence-graph.md
+# Candidate: typed evidence graph with constrained components
+
+## Problem
+
+Users need a funder search result that represents an organisation across normal source variation. The existing resolver drops cleaned components, treats punctuation in addresses as contradictory evidence, and makes source role part of identity. The replacement consumes cleaned features as evidence, derives audited identity components, and preserves every original observation and payment attribution. It does not use the uncalibrated Splink probability as an acceptance boundary. Database reconciliation is a separate deployment step; implementation does not mutate the existing imported database.
+
+## Usage (caller's view)
+
+Running declaration resolution produces canonical entities, source memberships, and explicit pair decisions. Searching `HSBC` returns one bank entity for spelling/case/legal-suffix variants, with the spellings as aliases. Searching `UNITE West Midlands` finds the parent union identity and retains the regional spelling on its declarations. A genuinely uncertain match remains a separate identity and appears in the review artifact.
+
+```rust
+// Resolution service: one domain operation after reading cleaned observations.
+let resolution = resolve_funders(cleaned_observations)?;
+storage.write_resolution(run_id, &resolution).await?;
+
+// Declaration loading: entity membership does not rewrite source attribution.
+let entity = resolution.entity_for(&payment.selected_funder_id)?;
+insert_payment(payment, entity.id());
+
+// Loader derives search aliases from entity evidence, never re-resolves identities.
+for entity in resolution.entities() {
+    insert_funder(entity.id(), entity.display_name(), entity.search_names());
+}
+```
+
+## Shape
+
+The domain owns a typed evidence graph. Nodes are cleaned source observations. Edges contain evidence and an outcome. Accepted edges form components, subject to component-level identity conflicts. This builds on the resolver's existing component shape instead of adding a second matching system. One entry point hides feature parsing, candidate indexing, classification, conflict checking, canonical naming, and audit construction; storage only translates artifacts. This is a deep interface with a short call chain, per minimize-reader-load and boundary-discipline.
+
+```rust
+pub fn resolve_funders(input: CleanedObservations) -> Result<Resolution, ResolutionError> {
+    todo!("build evidence graph, apply constrained components, derive output");
+}
+
+pub struct Resolution {
+    entities: Vec<ResolvedEntity>,
+    membership: BTreeMap<ObservationId, EntityId>,
+    decisions: Vec<PairDecision>,
+}
+impl Resolution {
+    pub fn entities(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &ResolvedEntity> { todo!() }
+    pub fn entity_for(&self, id: &ObservationId) -> Result<&ResolvedEntity, ResolutionError> { todo!() }
+}
+
+pub struct ResolvedEntity {
+    id: EntityId,
+    canonical_observation: ObservationId,
+    members: BTreeSet<ObservationId>,
+    search_names: BTreeSet<SourceName>,
+}
+
+// Private domain graph internals; callers cannot bypass acceptance policy.
+struct Observation {
+    id: ObservationId,
+    source: SourceProvenance,
+    role: FunderRole,
+    entity_class: EntityClass,
+    names: NameEvidence,
+    address: Option<AddressEvidence>,
+    company: Option<CompanyNumber>,
+}
+struct NameEvidence {
+    raw: SourceName,
+    normalized: NameKey,
+    organisation_core: Option<OrganisationKey>,
+    token_key: TokenKey,
+    explicit_aliases: BTreeSet<NameKey>,
+    explicit_acronym_expansion: Option<(AcronymKey, NameKey)>,
+    organisation_annotation: Option<OrganisationAnnotation>,
+    union_form: Option<UnionForm>,
+}
+enum UnionForm {
+    Root { distinctive_name: NameKey },
+    Branch { distinctive_name: NameKey, qualifier: BranchQualifier },
+}
+struct AddressEvidence {
+    punctuation_insensitive: AddressKey,
+    postcode: Option<Postcode>,
+    quality: AddressMatchQuality,
+}
+enum Evidence {
+    SameCompany(CompanyNumber),
+    SameName,
+    SameOrganisationCore,
+    ExplicitAlias,
+    ExplicitAcronymExpansion,
+    SameTokenSet,
+    SameUnionRoot,
+    UnionBranchOfRoot,
+    SameAddress,
+    DifferentAddress,
+}
+enum Decision {
+    Link(LinkBasis),
+    Review(ReviewReason),
+    Reject(Conflict),
+}
+enum LinkBasis {
+    CompanyAnchor,
+    OrganisationName,
+    DeclaredAlias,
+    CorroboratedName,
+    UnionIdentity,
+}
+enum Conflict { DifferentCompanies, PersonOrganisation, AmbiguousAnchor }
+enum ReviewReason { WeakName, UnprovenOrganisation, ConflictingAlias, ComponentConflict }
+
+struct EvidenceGraph {
+    observations: BTreeMap<ObservationId, Observation>,
+    edges: BTreeMap<OrderedObservationPair, EvidenceEdge>,
+}
+fn candidate_graph(input: CleanedObservations) -> Result<EvidenceGraph, ResolutionError> { todo!() }
+fn classify(edge: &EvidenceEdge, nodes: &NodePair) -> Decision { todo!() }
+fn components(graph: EvidenceGraph) -> Result<Resolution, ResolutionError> { todo!() }
+```
+
+`NameEvidence` reads cleaner-produced cores, alias forms, tokens, and validated acronym expansions. It derives organisation annotations and union forms in the resolution domain: cleaning remains evidence extraction, not policy. Company numbers are parsed at the input boundary, including zero-padding purely numeric UK numbers shorter than eight digits where the source field is explicitly a company number; malformed/alphabetic formats remain unanchored. Never pad arbitrary identifiers.
+
+Module map: existing `input.rs` parses cleaned wire data into these types; existing `identity.rs` owns all graph/evidence/component policy; existing resolution output owns artifact serialization. Keep feature logic private within the identity module until actual size justifies a private submodule. No separate generic rules framework, publicly configurable feature weights, or alias writer.
+
+### End-to-end flow
+
+1. Parse names, kinds, source roles, provenance, and company numbers at the input boundary. Withheld/missing names do not produce name edges.
+2. Build indexes in the graph builder for company number, normalized name, organisation core, explicit alias/expansion, union root, token key, and normalized address. Generate ordered unique pairs from those indexes within the existing candidate budget. Deterministic rules must receive candidates even when Splink does not generate them; Splink may supply additional review candidates only.
+3. Classify pair evidence. Address punctuation collapses before comparison; different addresses are neutral for organisations and supporting negative evidence for uncertain names, never an automatic organisation rejection. Roles describe attribution and do not prevent organisational identity merging.
+4. Build strong anchor/name components first. Then attach weaker accepted edges only if their entire target component has no conflicting company anchors or known person/organisation split. An unanchored component adjacent to two incompatible anchored components remains unmerged with both; do not choose whichever edge sorts first. Persist those candidate edges as review with a component conflict reason. This prevents a plausible bridge from silently merging two different companies.
+5. Derive deterministic run-local identity IDs and canonical names from members. Prefer a full unannotated organisation name, then legal-name specificity, then deterministic source ID; do not choose the shortest name blindly. Preserve raw names and explicit aliases as search names and every observation as membership evidence.
+6. Write memberships and decisions together as one resolution artifact set. Re-running the same input/policy is deterministic. Loading reads memberships without changing declaration source names or payer-selection logic.
+
+### Match, defer, reject policy
+
+| Evidence | Outcome |
+|---|---|
+| Equal valid company number | Link across organisation roles and addresses. |
+| Different valid company numbers or known person versus organisation | Reject; applies to whole components. |
+| Equal normalized organisation name or legal core | Link across roles; address changes are permitted. Unknown kinds need corroborating address, organisation-shaped name, or company evidence. |
+| Explicit trading-as alias or validated acronym expansion | Link compatible organisations; ambiguous/conflicting anchored targets remain review. Initials generated from a name alone never link. |
+| Equal token set | Link only compatible organisations with the same normalized address or explicit alias evidence; otherwise review. |
+| Union root variants with known trade-union kind | Link `Unite`, `Unite Union`, `Unite the Union`; connective/type tokens are removed only inside this typed union grammar. |
+| Union branch form with a matching union root observed in this run | Link regional and explicitly named branch variants into the union identity, retain the qualifier as source evidence. Two branch records without a root remain review unless otherwise corroborated. |
+| Same address alone, arbitrary fuzzy name, generic short name, unknown acronym | Review. |
+
+HSBC `PLC` and `plc` link immediately regardless of commas or attribution roles. `HSBC UK (Ian Stuart, CEO)` parses a representative annotation and matches a compatible bank organisation core when its company anchor or normalized address corroborates it. With neither corroboration, review rather than claiming the CEO personally is the bank. Parsing its seven-digit source company field as `09928412` makes the current anchor usable, but a conflict with an eight-digit bank record is visible and blocks merger. `HSBC Holdings` is a different core and does not merge on the acronym.
+
+Most listed Unite variants link via union-root and typed branch evidence. `United Against Malnutrition and Hunger` and the United Nations entry do not match the root token `unite`. The parent union search result keeps West Midlands, East Midlands, and Parliamentary Staff Branch spellings searchable, and those names remain visible on payments. This is an organisation-family identity policy for unions, not a claim that all internal branches are the same legal accounting body.
+
+## Synthesis decision
+
+Pending arena synthesis. This candidate's distinctive commitment is that accepted evidence forms constrained components, and pair decisions are derived from the same graph that determines membership. There is no separate search grouping layer.
+
+## Tradeoffs accepted
+
+- We accept union branches appearing under a parent union in exchange for useful entity search, while retaining branch attribution in source records.
+- We accept explicit domain grammars for union variants and representative annotations in exchange for stronger, explainable links than arbitrary token similarity.
+- We accept some remaining reviews in exchange for preventing a weak bridge from collapsing different company anchors.
+- We accept deterministic run-local IDs in this change in exchange for leaving persistent database reconciliation to an explicit migration rather than treating a rerun as safe replacement.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- Lowering the Splink threshold hides model calibration risk and exposes tuning to operators; it offers a small interface but no explainable acceptance boundary and cannot recover dropped features.
+- A search-only family projection hides duplicate rows in search while leaving funder pages, totals, and aliases inconsistent; it requires each caller to choose legal identity versus family identity. The graph centralizes that choice once.
+- A generic weighted feature engine supports many signals but exposes feature scales and thresholds as a second policy language. Typed evidence cases hide those details and make known source patterns directly testable.
+
+## Implementation reconciliation
+
+No implementation yet. The union-family decision is an explicit proposed product interpretation of the user's request. Reconcile any change to it before implementing its branch grammar and tests.
+
+## Open questions and risks
+
+- Should union branches ever require separate funder pages or totals? The proposed default groups them under the parent while retaining source branch names; if legal-entity accounting is required, a future family projection may be necessary.
+- Does the source company-number field consistently contain UK registration numbers, allowing numeric zero-padding? Verify its schema and representative data before accepting this parse rule.
+- Which representative annotations can be parsed without confusing a personal donation with an employer-funded benefit? Initially require explicit role markers such as CEO and independent company/address corroboration.
+- Could a very common short union root connect unrelated unions? Require observed trade-union kind, exact distinctive root token, and an observed root form; measure component growth and inspect new multi-anchor reviews on the real run.
+
+## Next implementation step
+
+Build behavior fixtures for the HSBC and Unite observations plus competing-company and unrelated-Unite-name negatives, then replace the existing acceptance classifier and deterministic candidate indexes against this contract.
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
Written to `/tmp/arena-loose-resolution/candidate-evidence-graph.md`.

The design uses typed evidence and constrained components, merges normal organisation spelling/role/address variants, groups typed Unite branch forms under the union, and preserves source attribution. Conflicting company anchors remain explicit reviews or rejections. Repository unchanged.
